 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Crystal Palace 1–3 Liverpool – Premier League Post-Match Report
 By Steven Smith
 After back-to-back defeats against Arsenal and Fenerbahçe, Liverpool travelled to Selhurst Park knowing that a response was needed. Andoni Iraola's side had endured a difficult week, with questions being raised about their energy, midfield balance and defensive organisation.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Reds delivered the result they needed, securing a 3–1 victory against a stubborn Crystal Palace side. It was not without its difficult moments, but there were plenty of encouraging signs as Liverpool returned to winning ways.
 The Starting Eleven
 Liverpool XI
 GK – Alisson Becker
 RB – Ronald Araújo
 CB – Jérémy Jacquet
 CB – Virgil van Dijk (c)
 LB – Milos Kerkez
 CM – Dominik Szoboszlai
 CM – Alexis Mac Allister
 RW – Cody Gakpo
 AM – Florian Wirtz
 LW – Bradley Barcola
 CF – Alexander Isak
 Substitutes Used
 Trey Nyoni → Dominik Szoboszlai (68')
 Víctor Muñoz → Bradley Barcola (68')
 Rio Ngumoha → Cody Gakpo (76')
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Lewis Koumas → Alexander Isak (90')
 Joe Gomez → Ronald Araújo (90+1')
 Goals
 Crystal Palace 0–1 Liverpool – Alexis Mac Allister (Dominik Szoboszlai) – 40'
 Crystal Palace 0–2 Liverpool – Florian Wirtz (Bradley Barcola) – 54'
 Crystal Palace 0–3 Liverpool – Alexander Isak (Bradley Barcola) – 89'
 Crystal Palace 1–3 Liverpool – Eddie Nketiah (Penalty) – 90+5'
 Match Statistics
 Possession – Crystal Palace 54% | Liverpool 46%
 xG – Crystal Palace 2.60 | Liverpool 2.65
 Total Shots – Crystal Palace 19 | Liverpool 20
 Shots on Target – Crystal Palace 7 | Liverpool 7
 Fouls – Crystal Palace 10 | Liverpool 18
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Corners – Crystal Palace 4 | Liverpool 7
 First Half
 Liverpool began the afternoon with a clear intention to put the previous week's disappointments behind them. Palace enjoyed periods of possession and looked to use their home advantage, but the Reds showed greater defensive organisation and determination than they had displayed in Istanbul.
 Alisson Becker was particularly important during the opening period, producing several excellent saves to keep the home side at bay. His contribution allowed Liverpool to remain patient and gradually find their rhythm.
 The breakthrough arrived in the 40th minute. Dominik Szoboszlai provided the delivery and Alexis Mac Allister rose to head home, giving Liverpool a valuable lead just before half-time.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It was an important goal at an important moment, rewarding a much-improved first-half performance.
 Second Half
 Liverpool started the second half with greater confidence and quickly doubled their advantage.
 Bradley Barcola supplied the assist for Florian Wirtz, who showed his clinical qualities with a well-placed finish in the 54th minute. The German's influence continues to grow under Iraola, and his ability to operate between the lines is becoming an increasingly important part of Liverpool's attacking play.
 The Reds made changes in the 68th minute, with Trey Nyoni and Víctor Muñoz replacing Szoboszlai and Barcola. The substitutions helped introduce fresh energy, while Liverpool continued to look dangerous on the counter.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The result was effectively secured in the 89th minute when Alexander Isak converted another Barcola assist to make it three. It was a much-needed contribution from the Swedish striker, who will be looking to build consistency and confidence in front of goal.
 There was a late blemish, however. Eddie Nketiah converted a penalty in the 90+5th minute, denying Liverpool a clean sheet after an otherwise encouraging defensive performance.
 Alisson had already produced an outstanding display and could do little to prevent the penalty from finding the net.
 Final Thoughts
 This was exactly the response Liverpool needed.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Following defeats against Arsenal and Fenerbahçe, there was a requirement to show greater intensity, concentration and togetherness. While Palace created opportunities and enjoyed more possession, Liverpool matched them in the important attacking statistics and made their chances count.
 Alisson was outstanding, Mac Allister delivered another important midfield contribution, and Wirtz showed the clinical edge that makes him such an influential player. Barcola also deserves credit for providing two assists, while Jacquet and Van Dijk offered greater defensive stability.
 There are still areas to improve, particularly in managing opposition pressure and maintaining concentration until the final whistle. The late penalty was an unnecessary frustration, but it should not overshadow a deserved victory.
 For Iraola, the most important outcome is the return to winning ways. The new system is still developing, and performances like this provide a platform to build upon.
 Three goals, three points and a much-needed response from the Reds.
 Steven Smith's Pre-Match Prediction:
 Crystal Palace 1–3 Liverpool
